title: So out of character
article: The final acts of Fred Preston are resting heavily on his family, for no bigger reason than they were so out of character for the man they knew.

A funeral was held Tuesday for the well-known 70-year-old Sundridge man whose name was whispered across the province of Ontario after he was revealed to be the lone suspect in the slaying of an OPP officer early last week. He died Thursday, March 11.
"I'm going to miss him a lot," said his brother Alex. "We were always pretty close. I saw him every two or three days and we were always working together."

Speaking with the Almaguin News the day before the funeral, Alex says he never knew his brother to be a person to lash out or speak in hatred of anyone and was still reaching for answers about the violence that ended not only Preston's own life but that he was alleged to have taken Constable Vu Pham's as well.

OPP report that on March 8, Pham was killed by the driver of a vehicle he had pulled over as part of a response to a 'domestic situation.' Another officer arrived at the scene and a shootout occurred in which a suspect was injured. The Special Investigations Unit later revealed the suspect to be Fred Preston and he was charged with first-degree murder and attempted murder on Wednesday, March 10. Sergeant Dave Rektor of the OPP Western Region Headquarters says the charge of first degree murder is automatically laid in what is suspected to be the deliberate killing of a police officer, whether premeditated or not.
Alex never thought that would be what his brother would be remembered for.
Fred Preston was the youngest of eight children - seven brothers and one sister -all of whom, except the eldest son, came north in 1943 from the Newmarket area to start a new life.
Preston, aged three or four when he arrived in the Sundridge area, soon took to the bush as he grew older and started working away from home.
"He always ran a chainsaw in the bush his whole life," said Alex, who says Preston was always good with his hands.

"He was a good carpenter and a good block layer. For a few years he laid block for houses from Huntsville to North Bay and everywhere in between. He laid the blocks for my daughter's house just this past summer," said Alex.
During the winter months Preston took to logging in the bush and through the 1980s and 1990s was joined by Alex, whom he worked for during construction season.
Over the past two years Preston got more and more into chainsaw carving, creating large sculptures out of wood, including horses, bears and wolves.

Fred Preston, like many of his siblings, was well known in the Sundridge area. He served as reeve of Joly Township from 1997 until 2003 and was a councillor there from 1991 until 1997. His sister is June Kent, mother of Mike Kent who founded Kent Trusses, a company he recently sold which employs 60 to 85 people in Sundridge, depending on the season. His brother Grant founded G.F. Preston Sales and Service, a well-known heavy equipment dealership in the area.
"We're close. We're all members of the same church," said Alex.

Not wanting to comment on the attention the family has received from provincial and national media, Alex says his home was also buzzing with calls from local residents who either know him and/or knew Fred and wanted to offer their support.
"The people around here have been very supportive. They have phoned me to offer their support and tell me how they couldn't understand how the Fred they knew could do this," said Alex.

Alex doesn't have much more in the way of explanation, but does say that Preston was experiencing medical problems, including diabetes and high blood pressure, and just a week before the incident near Winthrop had been struck by a series of dizzy spells that kept him in bed all day. He also added that Preston had been suffering from headaches since then.
"I guess we'll never know," he said.
Fred Preston is survived by his wife Barbara and daughters Cindy Desmarais, Penny Black and Anne Preston, along with five siblings.
